answer_summary: X is the product of NaIO4 cleavage of the seven C2-C3 vicinal diols of beta-cyclodextrin (7 alpha-D-glucopyranoside units), followed by NaBH4 reduction to -CH2OH arms and Ac2O/Py acetylation. The macrocyclic backbone (per unit: C1 - glycosidic O - C4 - C5 - ring O5) stays intact, so ring size rs = 7 * 5 = 35. Stereocentres: per unit C1, C4 and C5 remain stereogenic (the two ring-continuation ligands are diastereomorphic, CIP rule 5, because chiral X has no mirror/inversion symmetry) while former C2/C3 (now -CH2OAc arms) and C6 are CH2 and not stereogenic; sc = 7 * 3 = 21.
assumptions: The bracketed intermediate in the X arrow of the Q9-2 scheme is beta-CD with free 2,3-diols (7 units), consistent with page Q9-1 ('n = 7', '(OH)14', 7 x CH2OH).

Trusted general chemistry (allowed by candidate domain policy as trusted_general_law): NaIO4 cleaves vicinal diols (Malaprade) splitting C2-C3 into a dialdehyde; NaBH4 reduces aldehydes to primary alcohols; Ac2O/Py acetylates the free OH groups; glycosidic and ring ethers are inert to these reagents.

X is chiral (C7-symmetric, homochiral beta-D-glucose-derived units) with no mirror plane or inversion centre, so the two ring-continuation ligands at C1/C4/C5 are diastereomorphic and distinguished under CIP sequence rule 5 (the same reason the anomeric carbon of a native cyclodextrin is stereogenic).
